data.title: Regulation of 4E-BP1 phosphorylation: a novel two-step mechanism
data.authors: Gingras AC; Sonenberg N et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: 4E-BP1 is phosphorylated by an ordered, priming two-step mechanism that controls its release of eIF4E.
data.abstract_excerpt: The multisubunit eukaryotic translation initiation factor (eIF) 4F recruits 40S ribosomal subunits to the 5' end of mRNA. The eIF4F subunit eIF4E interacts directly with the mRNA 5' cap structure. Assembly of the eIF4F complex is inhibited by a family of repressor polypeptides, the eIF4E-binding proteins (4E-BPs). Binding of the 4E-BPs to eIF4E is regulated by phosphorylation: Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP isoforms interact strongly with eIF4E, whereas hyperphosphorylated isoforms do not.

extracted_findings.effect: 4E-BP1 phosphorylation follows a two-step mechanism that regulates its binding to eIF4E
